Why a roster can exceed 53: Up to two practice-squad elevations can expand the active/inactive roster to 54 or 55. This report uses observed ACT + INA, including those players. It does not force roster totals to 53.
Methodology, position estimates and limitations

ADL scope: Historical MFL weekly rosters for league 60206, seasons 2022–2025, weeks 1–17. The 2021 season is excluded because reconstructed Out labels substantially undercount MFL Out designations. Only ROSTER players count; taxi squad and ADL injured reserve are excluded. Players held on Active Roster with Suspended (S), Holdout (H), I, or any IR designation (including IR-R, IR-PUP and IR-NFI) are counted as Mispl. instead of ACT or INA, even on a bye. ACT + INA + Mispl. equals the ADL Active Roster total. Remaining Active Roster players with O/Out or a Bye are INA; everyone else is ACT. Historical MFL injury exports supply Out. All 68 displayed season-weeks use direct MFL injury records. Where those exports are empty or unavailable, archived nflreadr injury reports reconstruct Out; this is an estimate of the historical ADL designation. The local player audit identifies every source; the public coverage download reports designation sources by week. When MFL lists the same player under multiple roster statuses in one franchise-week, count the player once and prefer explicit ROSTER membership; conflicting source statuses remain in the local audit and weekly coverage totals. Byes come from the NFL schedule using same-week or nearest-week NFL team observations, with annual MFL team fallback flagged.

Comparison denominators: ADL averages include every franchise-week, including players on NFL byes. NFL averages include played team-games only. Both sides use weeks 1–17. These are comparable roster-position counts, but ADL INA is the requested Out/Bye definition, not an independently verified NFL gameday inactive list. Each franchise/team and season receives equal weight.

Roster scope: Completed regular-season team-games only. Byes and postseason are excluded. The canceled 2022 BUF–CIN game is excluded, so those teams have one fewer observed game in the comparison window. All original statuses are preserved in the source snapshot; only ACT and INA contribute to the composition benchmark. Status labels are source-reported and are not independently verified against gamebooks.

Averages: Count each player once per team-game, including zero position counts. Average games within each team-season, then give all 32 teams equal weight for the whole-NFL season. The displayed four-year composite equally weights the four season means. Values represent an average NFL team, not a sum across the entire league. Two decimals are presentation rounding.

Identity and position: Link nflreadr players to MFL IDs through GSIS, ESPN, Sportradar, PFR and Rotowire identifiers, plus direct ESPN/Rotowire identifiers in the annual ADL export. Conflicting candidates are not accepted. Use the matched MFL player’s position from that year’s league 60206 player export, never today’s position. Annual exports reflect the database as retrieved, not intra-season weekly MFL position history.

Fallback: For missing or unusable MFL matches, estimate from the most common MFL position among matched player classifications in the same season and NFL position/depth-position group. Count distinct player classifications, rather than weeks, when learning that schema. Save support and agreement share in the audit. If the group has no matched examples, translate FB→RB, K→PK, P→PN, NT→DT, ILB/MLB/OLB→LB and FS/SS→S; use the other explicit depth positions directly. Unresolved generic DB/DL stays UNMAPPED. NFL OL and LS remain non-ADL regardless of any MFL listing.

Remaining: ACT + INA − OL − LS. Any UNMAPPED players remain part of this total; their position is uncertain. This is an observed roster benchmark, not an adopted ADL roster rule or a reconstructed permanent 53-player roster.

Frozen snapshot: Refresh is explicit; ordinary dashboard builds reuse the saved data.

Sources: nflreadr weekly rosters, fantasy player ID crosswalk, NFL roster rules.

Coverage and methodology

Historical seasons cover weeks 1–17. The current season stops at the latest week present in the frozen NFL snap-count source. All regular-season team-games present in the source count; playoff games and NFL bye weeks do not. ADL submissions on franchise byes are included when a complete lineup is returned by MFL.

NFL players are linked through stable PFR/MFL IDs and assigned their season-specific league 60206 position. Missing matches use the most common ADL position among distinct matched players with that NFL position in that year; explicit NFL translations are the final fallback. Position-match coverage is available below. NFL side eligibility follows the ADL position: for example, a player listed as an ADL DT but used as an NFL fullback is not eligible for the offensive group. Annual player databases reflect positions when retrieved, not changes within the season.

The top-N cutoff follows the existing PositionLimits.R approach: players above the cutoff count fully and tied players split the remaining slots. Formation frequencies enumerate the possible integer position combinations among tied players, weighted by the number of player combinations. Their average position counts exactly reproduce the split-slot averages.

ADL uses MFL weeklyResults players marked “starter,” never the “shouldStart” optimal-lineup flag. Kicker, punter and non-individual positions are excluded. A complete offensive lineup has 7 relevant starters; a complete defensive lineup has 12. Missing or incomplete sides are excluded from averages and formation frequencies and reported in the coverage download. Both sources are averaged within each team, then equally across teams.

Source: nflreadr / PFR snap counts, public MFL weeklyResults and annual player exports.

Parity

How balanced are records and scores, and how quickly do stronger and weaker teams change places?

ADL H2H includes head-to-head games only. ADL Reg Season includes H2H plus Bonus Games. Completed seasons have 12 H2H games and 5 Bonus Games per franchise; season-to-date includes only Bonus Games already completed. Scoring margins remain H2H-only because Bonus Games have no opponent score margin.

Net margin is average points for minus points against, divided by the league’s average team-game score. It is expressed as a percentage of typical scoring.

Definitions, coverage and limitations

H2H columns count only actual head-to-head games. ADL Reg Season adds Bonus Games reconstructed using the local playoff-picture rules: rank cumulative all-play results, then points, then potential points for weeks 1–3, 4–6, 7–9, 10–12, and 1–12. Each event gives ranks 1–15 a win, 16–17 a tie, and 18–32 a loss. Only completed events count. Byes and postseason games are excluded. Bonus outcomes are correlated with scoring, so the coin-flip baseline is descriptive rather than a schedule model. ADL’s regular season is weeks 1–12, as defined in the existing playoff-picture script; historical MFL metadata incorrectly marks later contests as regular season and is overridden. Identical duplicate matchups count once; conflicting duplicates stop the build. NFL games without final scores, including the canceled 2022 Buffalo–Cincinnati game, are excluded.

Record spread is the population standard deviation of franchise winning percentages. The coin-flip baseline is √mean(0.25 ÷ games played), a conventional independent-game approximation rather than an exact schedule simulation. A ratio near 1 indicates about as much spread as this baseline; larger values indicate more imbalance. Ties count as half a win, with the .25 baseline retained as an approximation. Each team is equally weighted.

Normalized net-margin spread is the standard deviation across teams of their average signed margin divided by average league team-game points. Game-margin metrics use the same league-season scale. The close (≤25%) and lopsided (≥50%) thresholds are descriptive, not NFL possession rules. These ratios remove differences in score units but not every structural difference between NFL and fantasy scoring.

Yearly β is an ordinary least-squares slope with an intercept. Pooled record β first centers each league-season at its team-average winning percentage, then pools completed year pairs. Normalized net-margin β is also centered within each season before pooling. Gap reduction (1 − β) describes the fitted reduction in above/below-average separation; it is not the share of franchises that improved. Correlation measures association, not causation. Persistence and regression both reflect skill, roster turnover, management changes, schedule and sampling luck; they do not identify a scoring-rule effect.

Bottom/top quartiles contain eight team-equivalents in a 32-team league. Teams tied at a cutoff share membership rather than being separated alphabetically. “Winning” means strictly above .500 and “losing” strictly below .500. Franchise IDs track ADL teams across years; NFL team codes track NFL franchises. Ownership changes are not isolated. A 2026 partial-year comparison has fewer games and more noise, and never enters the completed-season pool.

Sources: public MFL weeklyResults, and nflreadr / nflverse game results.
